newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Computer 2000 sets delayed rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Computer 2000 sets delayed rights issue.

text.p: German computer wholesaler Computer 2000 on Tuesday set the terms for a rights issue that was initially announced in May, but then postponed.
The group said it would raise capital by 11.9 million marks ($8.1 million) to 47.7 million marks ($32.3 million), issuing one new share for every three old ones held.
The new shares, nominally valued at 50 marks a share, will be priced at 245 marks and the subscription period will run from September 4 to September 18, the group said in a mandatory statement.

After initially announcing its plans for a capital rise in early May, Computer 2000 decided, only two weeks later, to postpone the entire plan by three months. The basic conditions of the issue have not changed since then.
Computer 2000 said the reason for the postponement was that it wanted to first release results from the first nine months of its business year which will end on September 30.
It said earlier this month that nine-month sales jumped 37 percent to 5.1 billion marks. But profit dropped sharply to 13.3 million marks from 40.3 million marks in the full 1994/95 business year.
The company warned in August that this profit fall -- caused by a high tax bill and restructuring costs -- meant it was unlikelly to be able to pay a dividend for 1995/96.
It said today that the new shares would be eligible for 50 percent of any 1995/1996 dividend.
The company in early May said that the capital increase would be used to finance increasing business volumes, higher stakes in subsidiaries and move into new business fields.
